entries.en: While the data regarding the star systems as a whole was somewhat spotty, the detailed studies of individual planets has allowed the [Root.GetName] to extrapolate complete Survey data for the systems in question.

entries.zh: 赞。
entries.en: Fantastic.

entries.zh: 大灭绝：相信未来
entries.en: Mass Extinction: Future Faith

entries.zh: 随着越来越多有关研究的消息通过媒体传入民众的耳朵，人们越发变得焦躁不安。现在我们可以一次性打消他们所有的疑虑了。
entries.en: The populace has been growing increasingly restless as news of the study slowly filtered down through the media. Now, we have the chance to dispel all their doubts and fears in one fell swoop.

entries.zh: 母星安全了。
entries.en: The homeworld is safe.

entries.zh: 这是[Root.GetRulerTitle]领导下又一次成功的行动。
entries.en: Another successful operation by the [Root.GetRulerTitle].

entries.zh: 大灭绝：传播信息
entries.en: Mass Extinction: Information Dissemination

entries.zh: 科研探险中收集到的数据对[Root.GetName]来说弥足珍贵。因此，数据的使用也受到严格管控，以防某些欠缺考虑的事情发生。\n\n研究现已结束。为了科学的发展，很多人呼吁公开相关数据。
entries.en: The information gleaned by the research expedition is the property of the [Root.GetName] and access to it is restricted; a precaution put in place early on to prevent premature and unfavorable conclusions.\n\nWith the study now complete, there is a strong lobby for releasing all associated data to the wider scientific community.

entries.zh: 很好。
entries.en: Very well.

entries.zh: 接触报告：简单生命
entries.en: Contact Report: Simple Forms of Life

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]新闻满天飞，内容都是关于不久前发现的外星生物。\n\n尽管它离智慧生物还有很大差距，但至少说明外星是有生命存在的。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien organisms discovered some time ago.\n\nWhile far from intelligent, there is life out there.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]新闻满天飞，内容都是关于不久前发现的外星生物。\n\n尽管它离智慧生物还有很大差距，但至少说明外星是有生命存在的。这是一个无法回避的现实，人们开始担心未来。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien organisms discovered some time ago.\n\nWhile far from intelligent, there is life out there. An inescapable reality, and a deeply unsettling prospect.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]新闻满天飞，内容都是关于不久前发现的外星生物。\n\n这一生命的奇迹再次使[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的人们对第一次接触其他智慧生物满怀期待。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien organisms discovered some time ago.\n\nThese little evolutionary marvels kindle in the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] people a renewed hope of first contact with intelligent beings.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]新闻满天飞，内容都是关于不久前发现的外星生物。\n\n自从在[Root.Capital.GetName]之外发现了造物的奇迹，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]神秘学家们不断举办神秘仪式，试图得到更多的答案。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien organisms discovered some time ago.\n\n[Root.GetSpeciesAdj] theologians have been partaking in arcane rites since this first sign that divine providence extends outside of [Root.Capital.GetName], attempting to find new answers.

entries.zh: 我们确认了[Root.Capital.GetName]的生物圈之外存在低等有机生命。
entries.en: We have confirmed the existence of lower forms of organic life outside of [Root.Capital.GetName]'s biosphere.

entries.zh: 检测到有机异形微生物。已按情况调整存在有机智慧异形概率的算法模型。如果他们真的存在，他们将会被发现。他们将会被消灭。
entries.en: Alien microbes of an organic nature have been detected. Models for the probability of organic alien sapients have been adjusted accordingly. If they exist, they will be found. They will be exterminated.

entries.zh: 我们并不孤独。[Root.GetName]第一次确定了宇宙中有其他生命的存在；微生物、外星生命，但[Root.GetHomeWorldName]并不是唯一一个演化的舞台。\n\n一种莫名的饥渴从长久的沉眠中醒来，在我们的体内躁动不安地搅动。而我们的猎弓再度被拉开了。
entries.en: We are not alone. For the first time, the [Root.GetName] has definitive proof that there is other life in the universe; microscopic, alien life, but [Root.GetHomeWorldName] was not the only planet where evolution occurred.\n\nAn instinctive hunger, long dormant, begins to stir within us. Once again, we hunt.

entries.zh: 接触报告：深空住民
entries.en: Contact Report: Deep Space Dwellers

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]新闻满天飞，内容都是关于不久前发现的外星生物。\n\n这些生物似乎居住在深空之中。相比之下，[Root.Capital.GetName]上的极端微生物简直不值一提。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien organisms encountered some time ago.\n\nSeemingly native to deep space, they make the extremophile creatures of [Root.Capital.GetName] appear frail by comparison.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]新闻满天飞，内容都是关于不久前发现的外星生物。\n\n这些生物似乎居住在深空之中。相比之下，[Root.Capital.GetName]上的极端微生物简直不值一提。尽管有些人持怀疑态度，但是遇见外星生命基本是意料之中的事情。虽然如此，但[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]外星生物学家仍然抑制不住激动，对这种生命体所承受的种种极端条件感到兴奋不已。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien organisms encountered some time ago.\n\nSeemingly native to deep space, they make the extremophile creatures of [Root.Capital.GetName] appear frail by comparison. While some doubted, encountering alien life was ultimately expected and anticipated - but nothing could have prepared expectant [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] xeno-biologists for the fascinatingly extreme conditions in which this life thrives.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]上的人们平静地接收了对异常外星生物的报告。\n\n真空中真的存在生命这一事实在[Root.Capital.GetName]的科学界引起了短暂的争议。不过在此之前已发现过低等生命，因此所有的[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]都并未感到震惊。
entries.en: The subjects of the [Root.GetName] receive the report of the encounter with new and unusual alien beings with relative calm.\n\nThe supposed vacuum habitat of the aliens sparked some short-lived controversy in certain circles of the scientific community on [Root.Capital.GetName], but the previous discovery of lower forms of life had largely prepared all [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] for the shock.

entries.zh: 我们观测到了有机极端微生物在深空中遨游。
entries.en: We have observed extremophile organics navigating deep space.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]遭遇了太空有机体！我们的[GetScientistPlural]还不确定为什么体型如此庞大的生物能够在严苛的宇宙真空中央演化，也不知道这些极端环境中的生物可能拥有何种基因适应性。我们已经迫不及待想知道了。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] has encountered a space organism! Our [GetScientistPlural] do not yet know what caused such massive creatures to evolve in the harsh vacuum of space, nor what kind of genetic adaptations these extremophiles might possess. But we can't wait to find out.

entries.zh: 接触报告：行星动物
entries.en: Contact Report: Planetary Animalia

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]上新闻满天飞，内容都是关于发现的外星生物。\n\n尽管按照[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]标准来说，它们算不上是智慧生物，但它们的存在却否定了我们对生命的简单分类。它们提醒我们，宇宙是如此的复杂，蕴含了无尽的可能。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien life that was found.\n\nWhile hardly intelligent by [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] standards, the fascinating beings defy easy classification and hint at the immense complexities and possibilities of the universe.

entries.zh: [Root.Capital.GetName]上的教士们普遍对找到外星有机体——虽然较为低等——一事表示了认可。\n\n不过这一发现也引发了对教义的争论——这是可作为[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]是万物之主的证明，又或者我们只是还没有在深空之外遇见我们的同胞？
entries.en: The priesthoods on [Root.Capital.GetName] had a generally favorable reaction to the reports of complex - yet dumb - organisms found on alien planets.\n\nThe findings did spark some inter-doctrinal debate - is this proof that the [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are the lords of all within creation, or have we simply not yet encountered our brethren from beyond the void?

entries.zh: 在外星生物报告发布之后，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]外星生物学家欣喜地发现这一复杂的生命体与[Root.Capital.GetName]上的并没有太大的不同。\n\n这一生命物的出现否定了我们对生命的简单分类，但是它除了纯粹的动物本能之外也没有什么特别之处。尽管如此，它却告诉我们，生命的某些形式是普遍存在的。
entries.en: Following previous reports on alien life, [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] xeno-biologists are pleased to learn to complex life forms that appear not too different from what we would find on [Root.Capital.GetName].\n\nThe beings still defy easy classification and hardly possess anything more than purely animal instincts, but their existence does indicate that some patterns of life are indeed universal.

entries.zh: 我们在外星星球上发现了动物。
entries.en: We have confirmed animal life on an alien world.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]发现了新的复杂生命形式！这些生物可能不具备完全的只能，但我们的文明对各种各样的染色体样品总是来者不拒。\n\n我们的[GetScientistPlural]已经着手计算需要多少数量的基因物质才足够让我们所有的人口都分一杯羹了。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] has discovered a new form of complex life! These creatures may not possess true sapience, but our civilization has always enjoyed sampling from a wide range of genomes.\n\nAlready, our [GetScientistPlural] are calculating the amount of genetic material needed to provide everyone with a taste.

entries.zh: 接触报告：未开智生命
entries.en: Contact Report: Pre-Sapient Beings

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]上新闻满天飞，内容都是不久前遭遇的外星生物。\n\n这一生命体已经接近智慧生物了，真是令人兴奋不已。但我们也要清楚地认识到，尽管[Root.GetName]才刚刚登上星系的舞台，但这一切已经是相当大的进展。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien beings encountered some time ago.\n\nTheir near-intelligence is fascinating, and it is sobering to realize that while the [Root.GetName] may only just have made its entrance on the galactic stage, we have already come a long way.

entries.zh: 观测到外星动物一事在[Root.Capital.GetName]上造成了恐慌。视频中有一些东西——它们沉重的脚步和空洞的眼神——引起了[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]民众深深的不安。\n\n它们是不是外星的并不重要，重要的是外星生物学家们坚定地认为它们和我们非常相似。这简直就是一个扭曲的镜像，向[Root.GetName]展示着我们试图遗忘的，步履蹒跚的进化之路。
entries.en: The alien animals that were observed are cause for some consternation on [Root.Capital.GetName]. There is something in the video feeds - of their plodding gait and blank stares - that deeply disturbs the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] populace.\n\nPerhaps it is not their alien nature that concerns, but the xeno-biologists' insistence that they are very much like us. A warped mirror image of a shambling evolutionary past that the [Root.GetName] would rather forget.

entries.zh: 在遭遇外星生命后，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]新闻网铺天盖地的都是人们对此事的争论。\n\n该生物的智慧令人叹为观止。我们还要清楚地认识到，尽管[Root.GetName]才刚刚登上星系的舞台，但这一切已经是相当大的进展。大多数[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]都同意我们有责任和义务帮助其他的物种踏上同样的道路，不过前提是他们已经做好了准备。
entries.en: The [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] newsnets are ablaze with discussion and debate over the alien beings encountered some time ago.\n\nThe creatures' intelligence is fascinating, and it is sobering to realize that while the [Root.GetName] may only just have made its entrance on the galactic stage, we have already come a long way. Most [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] agree that it is an obligation and our moral duty to help other races make the same journey, when they are ready.

entries.zh: 遭遇外星生命后，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]宗教事务团体纷纷奔走相告。\n\n该生物的智慧令人叹为观止。我们还要清楚地认识到，也许[Root.GetName]才刚刚登上星系的舞台，但这已经是相当大的进展。[Root.Capital.GetName]上出现了激烈的争论，如果他们已经有了足够智慧并准备探索星空，我们到底应不应该为其引路。
entries.en: [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] congregations are buzzing with activity following news of the alien beings encountered some time ago.\n\nThe creatures' intelligence is fascinating, and it is sobering to realize that while the [Root.GetName] may only just have made its entrance on the galactic stage, we have already come a long way. There is heated debate on [Root.Capital.GetName] whether it would be our place to shepherd these creatures, should they ever achieve sapience and reach for the stars.

entries.zh: 多次发现低等生物后，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]首都收到的消息称他们观察到一种非常神奇同时具有莫大进化潜力的生物。\n\n此报告受到了极大的重视。
entries.en: Following previous discoveries of lower forms of life, the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] capital receives news of the observation of beings with impressive, if latent, cognitive capabilities and great evolutionary potential.\n\nThe report is received with marked enthusiasm.

entries.zh: 我们确认了即将进化出自我意识的外星生物的存在。
entries.en: We have confirmed the existence of alien lifeforms on the evolutionary brink of consciousness.

entries.zh: 我们发现了也只是全新的外星生命形式。这些生物比[GetHomeWorldName]上生活着的打大多数生命都要复杂，具有接近智慧水平的智力。我们已经开始建立必要的后勤和克隆程序来处理这些诱人的新基因组。
entries.en: We have uncovered a new form of alien life. These creatures are more complex than most of those that live on [GetHomeWorldName], with an intelligence that borders on sapience. We have already begun to establish the logistical and cloning routines necessary to process these tantalizing new genomes.

entries.zh: 接触报告：遗迹
entries.en: Contact Report: Remnants

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]的人对新近发现外星遗迹的消息议论纷纷。\n\n这些痕迹被视为外星人曾经存在并活跃过的铁证——我们现在虽然是孤独的，但至少我们不是第一个踏上星空的。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the alien remnants that were recently studied.\n\nThese remains are considered definitive proof of intelligent, purposeful alien activity at some point in the past - we may still be alone now, but we are at least not the first to be so.

entries.zh: [Root.Capital.GetName]上的有关部门对近日收到的关于外星遗迹的报告表示了一定忧虑。\n\n这些痕迹被广泛视为某种生命曾经活跃于宇宙的舞台上的铁证，不过一些著名的[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]专家认为这些痕迹其实只是地质构造现象或者大自然的自然变化。
entries.en: The administration on [Root.Capital.GetName] received the report on the alien remnants with some apprehension.\n\nThe remains in question are now widely considered to be definitive proof of unknown forces once having been active in the galaxy, though some prominent [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] thinkers reject this in favor of identifying the traces as "freak geological formations" or "results of curious natural phenomena."

entries.zh: [Root.GetSpeciesAdj]外星研究学家们很激动地发表了他们对近期外星生命发现的看法。\n\n这阵科学界的风暴对其他领域造成了暂时的负面影响。
entries.en: [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] xenologists are practically falling over themselves to publish their takes on the recent findings of alien life.\n\nThis fevered storm in the scientific community has had some negative, yet temporary, impact on pursuits in other fields.

entries.zh: “智能生物找不到伴”一则热门的新闻文章出现在[Root.Capital.GetName]上。[Root.GetName]的人们认为大家的注意力都集中在一些低等外星生物上，而真正有智能的外星种群却依然“戴着它们神秘的面纱”。\n\n最近发现关于外星生物痕迹的报告似乎只是为整件事情增添了一些讽刺意味。
entries.en: "Intelligent life taunts with pointed absence" reads a popular newsnet post on [Root.Capital.GetName]. The people of the [Root.GetName] are apparently finding some humor in the fact that lower forms of alien life are now a matter of public record, but potential equals from other stars continue to elude us.\n\nThe report on the traces of alien life that were recently found seemingly only add an ironic twist to the situation.

entries.zh: 我们在异星上发现了智慧外星生物存在的证据。
entries.en: We have confirmed the first material traces of intelligent alien life on a foreign world.

entries.zh: 接触报告：[GetPreFTLUpperPlural]物种
entries.en: Contact Report: [GetPreFTLUpperPlural]

entries.zh: 我们的舰队发现[GetPreFTLLower]外星文明的消息传遍了[Root.GetName]。\n\n虽然仍未掌握太空旅行的能力，但[primitive_planet.GetName]上的外星人已具有足够的智慧，而且他们的社会也具备了先进文明的所有特征。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] is abuzz with news of the [GetPreFTLLower] alien civilization found by our fleets.\n\nThey may not be capable of space-flight, but the aliens of the [primitive_planet.GetName] are quantifiably intelligent and their society shows all the hallmarks of a moderately advanced culture.

entries.zh: [GetPreFTLLower]生物，也就是所谓的[primitive_planet.GetName]文明，它们展现出基础智慧的新闻在[Root.Capital.GetName]上并不受人待见。\n\n一种深刻的不安情绪弥漫在公共辩论中，少数人大声疾呼，主张要不择手段建立[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]对外星星球的霸权，而大多数[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]似乎不愿意提起外星生物或完全忘记它们。
entries.en: News of the [GetPreFTLLower] creatures exhibiting rudimentary intelligence - the so-called civilization of [primitive_planet.GetName] - is not received well on [Root.Capital.GetName].\n\nA profound sense of unease permeates the public debate, as a vocal minority advocates establishing [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] hegemony over the alien planet by any means necessary, while most [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] would seemingly prefer to avoid the alien creatures or forget about them entirely.

entries.zh: 我们舰队观测到[GetPreFTLLower]文明的报告得到了[Root.GetName]上的学术精英们在维持自己体面的范围内最大限度的狂欢庆贺。\n\n于此，我们终于可以证明[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]走向漆黑星空的试探性一步并不会一无所获。他们也许暂时比不上我们，甚至我们这一辈的人都不会跟他们直接交流，但光是他们存在本身都是一盏能够照亮这个空荡荡静悄悄的宇宙的希望明灯。
entries.en: The report on the [GetPreFTLLower] civilization observed by our fleets is received with something as close to exultant jubilation as the academic elite of the [Root.GetName] will allow themselves to express.\n\nHere, finally, is proof that the first tentative [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] steps into the darkness of space were not for naught. They may not be our equals, not yet, and it may be that we will not interact directly with them in our lifetimes, but their mere existence is a beacon of hope in a galaxy that otherwise appears deadened and unmoving.

entries.zh: 发现智慧外星生命令[Root.Capital.GetName]的科学界欢呼雀跃。\n\n尽管仍未掌握太空旅行的能力，但[primitive_planet.GetName]上的外星人已具有足够的智慧，而且他们的社会也具备了先进文明的所有特征。著名外星研究学者表示，之前只能研究古代的遗迹，而现在确是一次研究外星社会的绝好机会。
entries.en: The scientific community on [Root.Capital.GetName] is excited to receive the report on intelligent alien life.\n\nThey may not be capable of space-flight, but the aliens of [primitive_planet.GetName] are quantifiably intelligent and their society shows all the hallmarks of a moderately advanced culture. Prominent xenologists note that this is an excellent opportunity to study a society perhaps not unlike the ones we have previously only found ancient remains of.

entries.zh: 发现[GetPreFTLLower]文化的报告受到了[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]研究者们的欢迎，而这一发现紧跟在发现未开化物种之后。\n\n[Root.GetName]目前是我们知道的首个踏上星空的文明，但是发现有其他文明仅仅落后我们数个纪元甚至只是数个世纪真的让人非常激动。
entries.en: The report on a [GetPreFTLLower] culture is welcomed by [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] researchers, following previous discoveries relating to pre-sapient species.\n\nAs far as we are aware the [Root.GetName] is the first civilization to take to the stars, but it is fascinating to learn that some other cultures may only be a few millennia, or possibly even centuries, behind.

entries.zh: 相比往常发现的非智慧生命，这次我们的舰队发现了[GetPreFTLLower]外星种群[primitive_planet.GetName]的报告无疑重新燃起了[Root.Capital.GetName]对外星科学的兴趣，在此之前这个领域向来被视为不过是纸上谈兵。
entries.en: Effectively capping off previous discoveries of lower forms of life, the report on the [GetPreFTLLower] aliens of [primitive_planet.GetName], encountered by our fleets has reignited interest in the xenological sciences on [Root.Capital.GetName], previously considered a largely theoretical field.

entries.zh: 我们确认了[GetPreFTLLower]外星文明的存在。他们仍不具备超光速旅行能力，被自身分裂的个性所阻碍。
entries.en: We have confirmed the existence of a [GetPreFTLLower] alien culture. They have yet to develop FTL capability, handicapped as they are by their fragmented individuality.

entries.zh: 我们发现了智慧生物！我们的一艘飞船遇见了一个[GetPreFTLLower]文明，这说明我们在虚空之中并不孤独。此外我们还缺人了他们的染色体很适合吸收。\n\n我们已经考虑了无数选项，包括精心计算的观测或者直接的入侵。我们的关系最终会变成什么样还有待观察，但种种可能性毫无疑问相当可口。
entries.en: We have discovered intelligent life! One of our vessels encountered a [GetPreFTLLower] civilization, which proves that we are not alone in the void. We have also confirmed that their genome is ripe for absorption.\n\nAlready, numerous options are being considered, from calculated observation to outright invasion. What form our relationship eventually takes remains to be seen, but the possibilities are certainly appetizing.

entries.zh: 接触报告：神秘的太空旅人
entries.en: Contact Report: Enigmatic Spacefarers

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]没过多久便遭遇了外星智慧生命。\n\n舰队发给[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]首都的报告很简单随意地描述了这些生物，还顺口提到了错失跟它们交流的机会。
entries.en: It did not take long for the [Root.GetName] to come across intelligent alien life.\n\nThe fleet's report to the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] capital somewhat understates just how alien these forces appear, and only in passing mentions the failure to open comms.

entries.zh: [Root.Capital.GetName]在收到发现未知飞船的消息后彻底沸腾了。\n\n目前尚不知道对方的目的，所以还是做好应对最坏情况的准备。
entries.en: [Root.Capital.GetName] is in an uproar following the news of unidentified ships sighted in the void.\n\nTheir intentions unknown, it would be prudent to assume the worst.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]终于遭遇了星空中的其他流浪者。\n\n虽然不知道这些外星人的意图，但是[Root.Capital.GetName]在收到舰队的报告后简直可用四海欢腾来形容。终于有人可以来见证一切了！
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] has finally encountered fellow wanderers among the stars.\n\nWhatever the intentions of these aliens, the atmosphere on [Root.Capital.GetName] can best be described as rapturous. At last, someone to bear witness!

entries.zh: 我们遭遇了可以进行太空航行的智慧生命。\n\n跟之前[Root.GetName]观察到的[GetPreFTLLowerPlural]物种不同，我们甚至还未能看清楚这些驾驶着飞船穿越深空的生物，也不清楚他们的目的。
entries.en: We have now encountered intelligent life capable of space-flight.\n\nIn sharp contrast to the [GetPreFTLLowerPlural] previously observed by the [Root.GetName], we have yet to get a good look at the beings piloting the crafts that move through the dark with purpose unknown.

entries.zh: 外星人飞船的消息传到了[Root.Capital.GetName]之后，可说是为[Root.GetName]踏往群星帝国的初章画上了一个圆满的句号。
entries.en: News of alien ships humming through the ether has reached [Root.Capital.GetName], in many ways ending the first chapter of the [Root.GetName]'s bid for a stellar empire.

entries.zh: 我们曾观察到拥有先进航天能力的外星飞船经过。尽管仍未与其取得联系，但可以确定我们[Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]并不是星系中唯一有能力探索太空的帝国。
entries.en: We have observed the passage of alien vessels capable of advanced spaceflight. While communications have not yet been established, we can confirm that we [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are not the only empire in the galaxy capable of stellar exploration.

entries.zh: 我们遭遇了高等外星生命。接触似乎不可避免。
entries.en: We have encountered advanced alien life. Contact seems inevitable.

entries.zh:
我们发现了具有太空航行能力的生命。

这一里程碑式的发现点燃了许多哲学和伦理争论：如果这些生物包含着能吸收的基因，我们应该强取豪夺，还是礼貌索要呢？只需要对自愿给予的样本进行克隆就足以满足我们整个人口所需的物质。

与这些有智慧的探索者们第一次接触的结果应该会帮助我们解答这些问题。
entries.en:
We have encountered life capable of space-flight.

This momentous discovery has accelerated many philosophical and ethical debates: if these creatures possess genes we can absorb, should we take them by force, or do we ask politely? Cloning freely-given samples could provide us with enough material for our entire population.

The result of first contact with these intelligent explorers should help determine the answer.

entries.zh: 猎物？
entries.en: Prey?

entries.zh: 新的生命能带来有价值的科学洞见。
entries.en: New life offers valuable scientific insights.

entries.zh: 我们与宇宙天人一体。
entries.en: We are one with the cosmos.

entries.zh: 做好接触潜在威胁的准备。
entries.en: Prepare to confront potential threats.

entries.zh: 生命的存在拓宽了我们的理解。
entries.en: The existence of life expands our understanding.

entries.zh: 多样性丰富了我们的集体智慧。
entries.en: Diversity enriches our collective wisdom.

entries.zh: 拥抱新生命的纽带。
entries.en: Embrace the bonds of new life.

entries.zh: 强化我们的防御以备不测。
entries.en: Fortify our defenses against the unknown.

entries.zh: 我们必须称霸寰宇。
entries.en: Our dominance must be asserted.

entries.zh: 准备整合它们的智慧。
entries.en: Prepare to integrate this intelligence.

entries.zh: 分析数据获得最优效率。
entries.en: Analyzing data for optimal efficiency.

entries.zh: 有趣。
entries.en: Intriguing.

entries.zh: 这是一个科学机遇。
entries.en: A scientific opportunity.

entries.zh: 无须担心。
entries.en: No cause for concern.

entries.zh: 这是潜在的威胁。
entries.en: A potential threat.

entries.zh: 共享知识的新可能性。
entries.en: A new potential for shared knowledge.

entries.zh: 必须维持好秩序。
entries.en: Order will be maintained.

entries.zh: 这是上天的旨意。
entries.en: A manifestation of divine purpose.

entries.zh: 新的开始。
entries.en: New beginnings.

entries.zh: 新的生命，新的威胁。
entries.en: New life poses unknown dangers.

entries.zh: 这种潜能是为集体智能而存在的。
entries.en: Potential exists for collective knowledge.

entries.zh: 信息已收集。
entries.en: Information gathered.

entries.zh: 接触报告：星神兽
entries.en: Contact Report: Leviathan

entries.zh: 在虚空中发现巨大生物一事使得[Root.GetName]在浩瀚之中显得更加微不足道了。我们伟大的帝国遇到的这第一只庞然大物很可能就是我们遭遇最后一只。这只巨兽的影像已经传遍了整个帝国，造成了极大恐慌，不少人要求政府采取行动。\n\n我方舰队的报告表明，这只巨兽的力量足以轻松摧毁宇宙中最为强大的舰队，建议我们小心行事。
entries.en: The discovery of a giant monstrosity living in the void has made the [Root.GetName] appear all the more insignificant in the grand scheme of things. The first creature our proud empire encounters might just be its last. The leviathan's image has spread across the empire, causing mass hysteria and pleas for action.\n\nOur fleet's report stated that the beast appears powerful enough to crush even the most capable armada, and recommends caution.

entries.zh: [Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的民众都在祈祷。黑暗中的巨怪使得帝国中的很多人开始质疑自己的神志是否清晰，甚至还有些人对神灵的宗教事务都开始动摇了。这些巨怪到底是生命的创造者和守护者，还是宇宙万物的敌人？
entries.en: The [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] populace is praying. The giant being encountered in the dark has caused many a denizen of the empire to fear for their sanity, or doubt their faith in the divine. Are these giants the guardians of all life and that which created it, or its enemy?

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]遇到了十分庄严崇高的存在。这种巨型生物的存在本身，就是宇宙孕育的无穷奇迹的最佳证明。在这巨型生物的身旁，任何生物都会显得无比渺小，一如腐草荧光安能与日月同辉。\n\n虽说这种巨型生物的行为方式尚不明确，[Root.Capital.GetName]的民众却在敬畏的同时抱有希望，对于这巨兽将带来的一切十分期待。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] has encountered something that is beyond sublime. Giant beings, their sheer existence a testament to the unfathomable wonders of the universe, that make most lifeforms appear like flickering lights next to burning stars.\n\nDespite the true nature of the leviathan being unknown, the people on [Root.Capital.GetName] are hopefully in awe of what has been found, and optimistic about what it may bring.

entries.zh: 在深空中发现特性不明的巨大个体迫使[Root.GetName]重新定义已知敌对单独个体的最大表面面积相关的参数。[Root.GetName]与新发现的该个体发生冲突时的生存率预测并不容乐观。\n\n建议科研与战斗单位继续观察，并对我们已有舰队的规格进行升级。
entries.en: The discovery of a massive entity with unknown properties in the void has forced the [Root.GetName] to redefine all known parameters for the maximum surface area of any single construct with hostile capabilities. Survival rate projections should the [Root.GetName] come into conflict with the newly discovered entity are not promising. \n\nScientific and military units recommend continued observation, and specification upgrades to our existing armada.

entries.zh: 我们找到了一些发展水平超越之前遭遇过的一切物种的生物。这种生物可以生长到前所未见的规模，体积和质量甚至可以与星球的卫星相比。\n\n真可谓是防不胜防。这一天将永远标示着[Root.GetName]历史的转折点。我们只希望我们种群还能存活到回顾此事的那一天。
entries.en: We have now found beings far surpassing anything encountered in our empire's spacefaring history. Life capable of growing to an unprecedented scale, rivaling moons in size and mass.\n\nNothing could have prepared us for this. This day will forever mark a turning point in the story of the [Root.GetName]. Let us hope we survive long enough to tell it.

entries.zh: 近期，有关一只巨兽出没在黑暗虚空之中的消息席卷了整个帝国。有人表示关注，有人表示乐观，但最多的人还是表示恐惧。历史文档中将会着重记录这重要的一天。
entries.en: News of a giant being seen in the dark void of space is spreading across the empire like a plague. There is concern and optimistic wonder, but mostly brings an existential dread to the populace. Historical documents will record this day as one of tremendous importance.

entries.zh: 有消息称在太空深处遭遇到了一个无比浩大的构筑，它正在延展贯穿整个[Root.GetName]。虽然它看起来并非是某种生物，不过其存在还是彰显了包含技术和巨型工程的可能性。
entries.en: News of the encounter with a deep-space construct of gargantuan proportion is spreading throughout the [Root.GetName]. While the entity does not appear to be of biological nature, its mere existence has inescapable ramifications for the possibilities of technology and mega-engineering.

entries.zh: 难道就只有这黑暗了吗？
entries.en: Is this darkness all that exists?

entries.zh: 我们只是尘埃虫豸之辈而已。
entries.en: We are but motes of dust.

entries.zh: 真是大开眼界啊。
entries.en: It is awe-inspiring.

entries.zh: 信息已收到。正在更新数据库。
entries.en: Information received. Updating databanks.

entries.zh: 考验我们信仰的魔鬼。
entries.en: Fiends to test our faith.

entries.zh: 神圣的证明。
entries.en: Proof of the divine.

entries.zh: 想想他们能教我们什么。
entries.en: Imagine what they could teach us.

entries.zh: 想象一下它们能成为多么壮观的战利品啊。
entries.en: Imagine how impressive of a trophy it could be.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫
entries.en: Space Amoebas

entries.zh:
我们的舰队不久前遇见的存在是一种全新的、美丽的、神奇的太空生命。

因为分析员对传感器数据的误读，这种生物很快就获得了“太空变形虫”的昵称，它们的体积比一般的[Root.Owner.GetAdj]护卫舰更巨大。

我们应该避免与它们接触，从[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]远距离观察这些生物。
entries.en:
The entities encountered by our fleets some time ago are new, wondrous, forms of spaceborne life.

Quickly nicknamed "Space Amoeba" following an analyst's gross misreading of initial sensor output, the creature is in fact larger than the average [Root.Owner.GetAdj] corvette.

We should leave it be and remotely monitor the creature and its kin from [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

entries.zh:
我们的舰队不久前遇见的存在是一种全新的、骇人的太空生命。

因为分析员对传感器数据的误读，这种生物很快就获得了“太空变形虫”的昵称，它们的体积比一般的[Root.Owner.GetAdj]护卫舰更巨大。

终结这些憎恶异形苟活于世的苦难应该没有什么害处。

既是为了科学，也可以是为了其他什么。
entries.en:
The entities encountered by our fleets some time ago are new, horrifying lifeforms.

Quickly nicknamed "Space Amoeba" following an analyst's gross misreading of initial sensor output, the creature is in fact larger than the average [Root.Owner.GetAdj] corvette.

There would be little harm in putting the monstrosities out of their misery.

For science, or some equivalent.

entries.zh:
我们的舰队不久前遇见的存在是一种太空生命。

因为分析员对传感器数据的误读，这种生物很快就获得了“太空变形虫”的昵称，它们的体积比一般的[Root.Owner.GetAdj]护卫舰更巨大。

这些生物对[Root.Owner.GetAdj]舰船表现出了敌意的行为，但我们授权进一步的研究。
entries.en:
The entities encountered by our fleets some time ago are spaceborne forms of life.

Quickly nicknamed "Space Amoeba" following a tactician's gross misreading of initial sensor output, the creature is in fact larger than the average [Root.Owner.GetAdj] corvette.

The creature displays aggressive behavior towards [Root.Owner.GetAdj] ships but further study might be warranted.

entries.zh:
我们的舰队不久前遭遇的是一种从未见过的太空生命。

因为分析员对传感器数据的误读，这种生物很快就获得了“太空变形虫”的昵称，它们的体积比一般的[Root.Owner.GetAdj]护卫舰更巨大。

虽然它脾气很坏，但是想进一步研究也不是不行的——我们可以从[Root.Owner.Capital.GetName]远距离观察它们。
entries.en:
The entities encountered by our fleets some time ago are new, spaceborne lifeforms.

Quickly nicknamed "Space Amoeba" following an analyst's gross misreading of initial sensor output, the creature is in fact larger than the average [Root.Owner.GetAdj] corvette.

Despite its apparent orneriness, further study is warranted - we can remotely monitor the creature and its kin from [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

entries.zh: 我们的舰队不久前遇见的存在是一种全新的太空生命。\n\n尽管个体体型远远大于[Root.Owner.GetAdj]的护卫舰，这些“太空变形虫”兽群相对于我们的舰队依然弱小不堪。
entries.en: The entities encountered by our fleets some time ago are new, spaceborne lifeforms.\n\nWhile significantly larger than a [Root.Owner.GetAdj] Corvette, these "Space Amoeba" herds are minuscule next to our full corpus.

entries.zh: 发布一项远距离研究太空变形虫的特殊计划。
entries.en: Issue a special project for remote Space Amoeba study.

entries.zh: 我们的舰队应该能够快速击杀这只生物。
entries.en: We expect our fleets to make short work of the creature.

entries.zh: 永远的太空变形虫
entries.en: Space Amoebas Forever

entries.zh:
太空变形虫——这个昵称现在已经传遍了[Root.Capital.GetName]的大街小巷——是一种独居的生物。成年的太空变形虫身边总会伴随着一种被称为鞭毛的半独立生物。鞭毛由变形虫自行生成，并通过分泌液态RNA来进行控制。

我们一度误以为这就是太空变形虫的幼体，但其实这些鞭毛并不含有繁殖器官，每个鞭毛更像是变形虫向外延伸的肢体。这些鞭毛可以在一定范围内离开主体并攻击敌人，但每隔一段时间就需要回返主体内进行重构。

太空变形虫厚皮的再生特性，或鞭毛的精巧的运动模式都有着潜在的军事应用价值。
entries.en:
The Space Amoebas - the nickname now lovingly popularized on [Root.Capital.GetName] - are solitary animals, when left to their own devices. All but the youngest specimens are accompanied by quasi-independent organisms, dubbed flagella, seemingly spawned by the Amoeba and programmed through liquid, RNA-laced secretions to do the bidding of the host.

Initially assumed to be young Space Amoebas, the flagella do not seem to factor into any reproductive mechanics, each individual flagellum instead operating solely as a disconnected limb for its host Amoeba. These flagella are capable of manipulating and even attacking objects in an impressive yet restricted range around the host, periodically returning to lodge inside the host Amoeba's body for re-programming.

There are potential military applications to be found in the regenerative properties of the amoeba's thick hide, or in the flagella's graceful patterns of movement.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫——这个昵称在这些生物被发现之后，在[Root.Capital.GetName]彻底火起来了。它们是一种独自生活的生物。成年的太空变形虫的身边会伴随着一种被称为鞭毛的半自主生物。鞭毛是由太空变形虫所生成，并通过液态RNA分泌物来控制。\n\n鞭毛一度被误会为太空变形虫的幼体，但其实它们并不含有繁殖器官，每个鞭毛更像是太空变形虫主体身上断开的肢体一般。这些鞭毛可以在离开主体的一定范围内攻击敌人，但每隔一段时间就需要回返太空变形虫体内被重新编译。
entries.en: The Space Amoebas - the nickname became popular after the story of how it came to be found its way back to [Root.Capital.GetName] - are solitary animals, when left to their own devices. All but the youngest specimens are accompanied by quasi-independent organisms, dubbed flagella, seemingly spawned by the Amoeba and programmed through liquid, RNA-laced secretions to do the bidding of the host.\n\nInitially assumed to be young Space Amoebas, the flagella do not seem to factor into any reproductive mechanics, each individual flagellum instead operating solely as a disconnected limb for its host Amoeba. These flagella are capable of manipulating and even attacking objects in an impressive yet restricted range around the host, periodically returning to lodge inside the host Amoeba's body for re-programming.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫——当为这种外星生物运用合适的分类方法来确定学名太过麻烦时，这个名称就被[Root.GetSpeciesName]的普罗大众沿用下来——是一种在太空中独居的生物。除了最幼小的那些个体以外，所有我们收集到的样本都拥有半独立的鞭毛和其他有机质，它们由变形虫本身产生并在液态的RNA分泌物中被设计，以方便宿主操纵。这些鞭毛可以被宿主操纵，甚至可以攻击宿主周围巨大但有限范围内的物体，并会定期的缩回变形虫体内，并被重新设计。\n\n太空变形虫厚皮的再生特性，或鞭毛的精巧的运动模式都有着潜在的军事应用价值。
entries.en: The Space Amoebas - the name has stuck as the pronunciation of the proper xeno-taxonomic denominator is too unwieldy for the average [Root.GetSpeciesName] - are solitary animals, when left to their own devices. All but the youngest specimens are accompanied by quasi-independent flagella, organisms spawned by the Amoeba and programmed through liquid, RNA-laced secretions to do the bidding of the host. These flagella are capable of manipulating and even attacking objects in an impressive yet restricted range around the host, periodically returning to lodge inside the host Amoeba's body for re-programming.\n\nThere are potential military applications to be found in the regenerative properties of the amoeba's thick hide, or in the flagella's graceful patterns of movement.

entries.zh: 一只太空变形虫通常伴随着一些半自主的鞭节，用于防御以及移动物体。变形虫与其鞭节并不共享意志，而是前者使用一种带有核糖核酸的分泌物来为后者编程，指引其完成较为复杂的任务。
entries.en: A Space Amoeba is usually accompanied by a handful of semi-independent flagella used for defense and object manipulation. The Amoeba and its flagella do not share a mind, the former instead using RNA-laced secretions to program the latter for the execution of tasks of middling complexity.

entries.zh: 确实神奇。
entries.en: Fascinating indeed.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫已解剖
entries.en: Space Amoeba Dissected

entries.zh:
太空变形虫——现在已经是负责捕猎它们的[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]部队口中的贬义词——它们比预想中更加复杂。它们的坚硬外壳保护着体内的无数小型太空变形虫，这些小型个体可比喻作保护着它们的太空变形虫母飞船的攻击机。这些攻击型太空变形虫虽然跟正常的太空变形虫很相似，但其实它们是相对简单的生物。太空变形虫体内拥有成千上百个器官，无疑都是存活于恶劣的太空环境的必要零件。

在分尸太空变形虫身体时，这些器官大部分都要么破裂了要么被烧坏了，只留下了残缺的尸体。

不过，参与太空变形虫项目的外星研究学家认为获取样本的过程是很重要的，所以他们发布了特殊的开火命令给整支舰队。只要针对五只或更多太空变形虫的特殊部位进行手术式打击，我们就能重组一个完整的尸体。
entries.en:
The Space Amoebas - now a quasi-derogatory term gleefully popularized by the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] forces tasked with bringing them down - are much more complex than anticipated. Their hardy exteriors protect a great number of pockets housing smaller "amoebas," creatures that our fleets have observed effectively acting as strike craft when engaging the "mothership amoeba." While superficially similar beyond the obvious differences in size, the "strike amoeba" are much simpler creatures than the Space Amoeba proper. Inside the Space Amoeba, beyond these pockets, lie hundreds of delicate organs doubtlessly all integral to surviving the harsh vacuum of space.

Many of these organs ruptured or were simply incinerated in the process of dispatching the Amoeba, leaving us with a largely incomplete carcass.

However, xeno-biologists assigned to the Space Amoeba project believe that the process of acquiring specimens is sound, and have distributed specific targeting instructions among the military fleets involved. With five more Amoebas, killed by surgical strikes to specific parts of their anatomy, a complete carcass can effectively be reconstructed.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫——一个虽然违背了[Root.Owner.Capital.GetSpeciesAdj]传统的分类命名法但已经深入人心的名字——它们比预想中更加复杂。它们的坚硬外壳保护着体内的无数小型太空“变形虫”，这些小型个体可比喻作保护着它们的太空变形虫“母飞船的攻击机”。这些“攻击型太空变形虫”虽然跟正常的太空变形虫很相似，但其实它们的生理构造相对简单。太空变形虫体内拥有成千上百个器官，无疑都是存活于恶劣的太空环境的必要零件。在解决太空变形虫时，这些器官大部分都要么破裂了要么被烧坏了，只留下了残缺的尸体。但是，太空变形虫项目组的外星生物学家认为这已经足够了，他们成功辨识出了太空变形虫的生理特征和独特弱点。
entries.en: The Space Amoebas - as they defy easy classification according to traditional [Root.Owner.Capital.GetSpeciesAdj] taxonomy, the name has stuck - are much more complex than anticipated. Their hardy exteriors protect a great number of pockets housing smaller "amoebas," creatures that our fleets have observed effectively acting as strike craft when engaging the "mothership amoeba." While superficially similar beyond the obvious differences in size, the "strike amoeba" are much less physiologically complex than the Space Amoeba proper. Inside the Space Amoeba, beyond these pockets, lie hundreds of delicate organs doubtlessly all integral to surviving the harsh vacuum of space. Many of these organs ruptured or were simply incinerated in the process of dispatching the Amoeba, leaving us with a largely incomplete carcass. Xenobiologists assigned to the Space Amoeba project believe this to be enough however, as they have already successfully identified several physiological features and weaknesses unique to the Space Amoebas.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫比当初预料的更为复杂。它们坚硬的外壳保护着大量装有小型“变形虫”的口袋，我们的舰队在与“变形虫母船”的交战中观察到它们实际上充当了攻击机。尽管除了尺寸以外它们在外表上大致相同，“攻击变形虫”在结构上比真正太空变形虫要简单得多。在太空变形虫体内的这些口袋后面，有着数以百计的脆弱器官，无疑都是为了在严酷的太空环境中生存。在与变形虫交战的过程中很多器官都破损或是被烧毁了，因此我们只获得了残缺不全的尸骸。不过负责太空变形虫计划的外星生物学家认为这就已经足够了，因为他们已经成功地鉴别出了太空变形虫数个独特生物特征以及弱点。
entries.en: The Space Amoebas are much more complex than anticipated. Their hardy exteriors protect a great number of pockets housing smaller "amoebas," creatures that our fleets have observed effectively acting as strike craft when engaging the "mothership amoeba." While superficially similar beyond the obvious differences in size, the "strike amoeba" are much less physiologically complex than the Space Amoeba proper. Inside the Space Amoeba, beyond these pockets, lie hundreds of delicate organs doubtlessly all integral to surviving the harsh vacuum of space. Many of these organs ruptured or were simply incinerated in the process of dispatching the Amoeba, leaving us with a largely incomplete carcass. Xenobiologists assigned to the Space Amoeba project believe this to be enough however, as they have already successfully identified several physiological features and weaknesses unique to the Space Amoebas.

entries.zh: 想方设法尽快消灭它们。
entries.en: Whatever helps us be rid of them faster.

entries.zh: 打靶练习。
entries.en: Target practice.

entries.zh: 很好。
entries.en: Very well.

entries.zh: 太空变形虫已被消灭
entries.en: Space Amoebas Slaughtered

entries.zh: 杀了数个太空变形虫后，我们终于能够研究太空变形虫跟它体内的小型生物的诡异关系。[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的外星生物学家发现，这些以它们的行动方式来命名的条状体不是什么太空变形虫幼体也不是寄生物。它们仅仅是在主体成年后生成的工具。它们被委派的任务一旦完成，就会返回到太空变形虫主体的一个口袋结构内。它们既是操纵者同时也是主体伸向无边黑暗的附属物。它们唯一的弱点在于接受命令时的反应延迟，不过这一点被人海战术、个体的反射性反应、以及自动追踪太空变形虫主体的特点所弥补了。\n\n无论如何，我们还是尽快杀了它们吧。
entries.en: Several dead Amoebas later, we are able to investigate the Space Amoebas' grotesque relationship with the smaller creatures they house inside their bodies. As far as [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] xeno-biologists can tell, these flagella - named for their whip-like movements - are not proper offspring or even parasites. They are simply spawned from the host once the host reaches maturity, created as tools rather than the result of procreation. Once their task is complete they return to a pocket in the host Amoeba, seemingly to receive new orders. They work as manipulators, blind appendages reaching in the dark. The laughably obvious drawbacks resulting from their inherently delayed reaction time are somewhat offset by the Amoeba's sheer number of circulating flagella, and the individual flagellum's strong set of reflexive responses and ability to dumbly track the host Amoeba.\n\nAt any rate, we are better at killing them now.

entries.zh: 采集了数个残骸后，我们能够研究太空变形虫跟它体内的小型生物的奇特关系。[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的外星生物学家发现，这些以它们的行动方式来命名的条状体不是什么太空变形虫幼体也不是寄生物。这些条状体没有脑袋，而是拥有一个复杂的颗粒状处理器中心。这个中心负责解码皮层下的接收器所接收到的来自太空变形虫的RNA的命令。它们被委派的任务一旦完成，就会返回到太空变形虫主体体内并开始接受新的任务。它们是士兵、炮灰、工具、侦查员。它们唯一的弱点在于接受命令时的反应延迟，不过这一点被人海战术、个体的反射性反应、以及自动追踪太空变形虫主体的特点所弥补了。太空变形虫的深空战斗效率主要是依靠它们不断释放的条状体，这一点可供我们的部队学习。
entries.en: With several carcasses collected, we are able to investigate the Space Amoebas' curious relationship with the smaller creatures they house inside their bodies. As far as [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] xeno-biologists can tell, these flagella - named for their whip-like movements - are not proper offspring or even parasites. They are simply spawned from the host once the host reaches maturity, created as tools rather than the result of procreation. Where one would expect to find a brain - considering their intricate movement and inter-flagellar interactions - the flagellum instead possess a complex glandular processing center. This center decodes input - orders - in the form of RNA, secreted by the Amoeba and received by the flagellum through subcutaneous receptors. Once their task is complete they return to a pocket in the host Amoeba to receive new orders. This allows them to work as manipulators, hands severed from the body. The obvious drawbacks in this inherently delayed reaction time are somewhat offset by the Amoeba's sheer number of circulating flagella, and the individual flagellum's strong set of reflexive responses and ability to dumbly track the host Amoeba. The Space Amoebas' relative proficiency in deep-space combat is largely due to the consistent deployment of their flagella, something our forces could likely learn a lot from.

entries.zh: 击杀第四只生物后，一个完整的太空变形虫尸体终于在[Root.GetName]capital[Root.Capital.GetName]重组完毕了。我们现在开始将揭示这种生物的秘密，然后将收获的信息分发到[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]帝国的相关部门中。\n\n当前最有价值的发现莫过于太空变形虫的皮肤膜。它们能够吸收——然后通过复杂的精确流程——消化无数种宇宙辐射，甚至把这些射线转化为营养。
entries.en: Following the slaying of the fourth creature, a complete Space Amoeba carcass was reconstructed on the [Root.GetName]'s capital of [Root.Capital.GetName]. We are now beginning to divine some of the creatures' hidden truths, and they are being conveyed to the appropriate departments within [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] administration.\n\nThe perhaps most useful discovery at present relates to the Space Amoebas' cutaneous membranes. They absorb and - through complex glandular processes - metabolize a wide range of cosmic radiation, seemingly drawing some sustenance from the rays.

entries.zh: 确实如此。
entries.en: Righteous.

entries.zh: 应该学习一下。
entries.en: Then learn we shall.

entries.zh: 这样的知识很有用。
entries.en: This knowledge can be put to good use.

entries.zh: 晶态实体
entries.en: Crystalline Entities

entries.zh: 我们的[This.Owner.GetResearchers]已经完成了对这种在[This.System.GetName]恒星系发现的非凡的、自由漂浮的晶态物体的调查报告。他们的发现令人震惊。
entries.en: Our [This.Owner.GetResearchers] have finished investigating the reports of extraordinary, free-floating crystal-like objects observed in the [This.System.GetName] system. Their findings are startling.

entries.zh:
$story.201.desc.base$

这些飞船般大小的物体以及它们的较小型的晶体卫星初看之下是无生命迹象的，然而一旦我们飞船靠近，它们就会突然改变方向并且从晶体内散发出能源波动，这说明它们也许是以生命形式存在的——这样的现象毫无疑问令人好奇，但我们得要小心处理。

我们最杰出且聪敏的科学家们都准备好研究这些实体了。
entries.en:
$story.201.desc.base$

The ship-size objects and their slightly smaller but equally crystal-like satellites at first appeared inert, but sudden shifts in their orientation relative to our ships and new energy signatures emerging from within the prisms indicate that they might be alive - a fascinating prospect to be sure, but they should be approached with caution.

Our best and brightest are standing by to study these entities.

entries.zh:
$story.201.desc.base$

这些飞船般大小的物体以及它们的较小型的晶体卫星初看之下是无生命迹象的，然而一旦我们飞船靠近，它们就会突然改变方向并且从晶体内散发出能源波动，毫无疑问它们具有可能的危险性，我们应该小心应对。

我们最好派遣一支舰队试探这些晶体的侵略性，如果发现有威胁就把它们摧毁掉。
entries.en:
$story.201.desc.base$

The ship-size objects and their slightly smaller but equally crystal-like satellites at first appeared inert, but sudden shifts in their orientation relative to our ships and new energy signatures emerging from within the prisms indicate that they should be regarded as hazardous and approached with extreme caution.

We should deploy a fleet to gauge the crystals' offensive strength, should they possess any, and destroy them if they are a threat.

entries.zh:
$story.201.desc.base$

这些飞船般大小的物体以及它们的较小型的晶体卫星初看之下是无生命迹象的，然而一旦我们飞船靠近，它们就会突然改变方向并且从晶体内散发出能源波动，它们毫无疑问具有可能的危险性，我们应该小心应对。

既然我们不想冒险得罪这些晶体，那就从首都远距离监视它们吧。
entries.en:
$story.201.desc.base$

The ship-size objects and their slightly smaller but equally crystal-like satellites at first appeared inert, but sudden shifts in their orientation relative to our ships and new energy signatures emerging from within the prisms indicate that they should be regarded as hazardous and approached with caution.

As we do not wish to risk coming into conflict with these prismatic enigmas, we ought to establish remote surveillance and observe them from the capital.

entries.zh:
$story.201.desc.base$

这些飞船般大小的物体以及它们的较小型的晶体卫星初看之下是无生命迹象的，然而一旦我们飞船靠近，它们就会突然改变方向并且从晶体内散发出能源波动，毫无疑问它们对[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]的飞船产生了反应。

这些晶体的生性和来历不明，但它们的形态与不加矫饰的棱角都与[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]的灵魂产生了共鸣。[Root.Owner.GetName]应当退一步，从远距离和平地观察它们。
entries.en:
$story.201.desc.base$

The ship-size objects and their slightly smaller but equally crystal-like satellites at first appeared inert, but sudden shifts in their orientation relative to our ships and new energy signatures emerging from within the prisms indicate that they are reacting to the presence of [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] ships.

The nature and origin of these crystals elude us at present, but there is something in their shape, their pristine angles, that resonates with the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] soul. The [Root.Owner.GetName] ought to take a step back, and observe from a respectful distance.

entries.zh:
$story.201.desc.base$

这些飞船般大小的物体以及它们的较小型的晶体卫星初看之下是无生命迹象的，然而一旦我们飞船靠近，它们就会突然改变方向并且从晶体内散发出能源波动，毫无疑问它们具有可能的危险性，我们应该小心应对。

哪怕找不到什么战斗用途，我们研究一个被击碎的晶体肯定也会有一些有趣的发现。
entries.en:
$story.201.desc.base$

The ship-size objects and their slightly smaller but equally crystal-like satellites at first appeared inert, but sudden shifts in their orientation relative to our ships and new energy signatures emerging from within the prisms indicate that they should be regarded as hazardous and approached with caution.

Even should we not find a martial use for them, studying a shattered crystal would no doubt yield interesting results.

我们既可以选择直接与这些危险的生命体交火，也可以从远距离安全地观察它们。

The ship-size objects and their slightly smaller but equally crystal-like satellites at first appeared inert, but sudden shifts in their orientation relative to our ships and new energy signatures emerging from within the prisms indicate that they should be regarded as hazardous and approached with caution.

We can either attempt to engage with the potentially dangerous objects directly, or establish remote surveillance and observe them from a safe distance.

entries.zh: 不灭晶体
entries.en: Crystalline Entities Are Unbreakable

entries.zh:
晶态实体——这是[Root.Capital.GetName]的外星生物学家跟外星地质学家互相妥协后所决定的名字——它们确实是生命体。

一部分过于保守的[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]学术精英认为它们是“硅酸盐活性物质”，跟生命体没什么共同之处。

[Root.GetName]的大部分民众不认同这种观点，而是开始赞叹这种晶态实体所代表的新概念。它们是一种单独生活的生物，每一个母体结晶通常只会带着一个哨兵以及一小队晶体军团。除了明显服从领袖命令的哨兵和军团之外，我们对于晶态实体的社会分层是一无所知——这个课题在[Root.Capital.GetName]引发了一场热烈探讨。

晶体似乎不会繁殖，而且我们还没有发现它们的个体之间有明显的年龄差别。跟早前的推论不同，晶体的不同颜色与它们的年龄无关，而是受到内部的潜在变化而改变——而这种变化可以被释放出来——这种偶尔的波动会改变晶体的反射属性。
entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities - the name itself a compromise between rival factions of xeno-biologists and xeno-geologists on [Root.Capital.GetName] - are most definitely alive.

Some overly-conservative members of the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] academic elite argue that they are "silicate-animate matter," and that they have little in common with biological life.

Most of the [Root.GetName] populace rejects that regressive perspective, instead turning their view toward the fascinating new horizons that the Crystalline Entities represent. They are, somewhat regrettably, solitary beings, each individual Crystal Sovereign rarely seen with more than one Sentinel and a smaller Cohort entity. Aside from the Cohort and Sentinel clearly being subservient to the Sovereign of the group, the subtle nuances of the Crystalline Entities' socio-hierarchical relationships are lost on us - which does not stop these dynamics from being the subject of fevered study on [Root.Capital.GetName].

The Entities do not seem to mate, and we have yet to observe any Crystals that are recognizably older or younger than others. Contrary to an early hypothesis, the shifts in hue between individual Crystalline Entities seem to be related not to their age but to their latent internal charge - which can be violently unleashed - and it appear as if though sporadic fluctuations in this charge alter the refractive properties of the Crystal.

entries.zh:
晶态实体——这是[Root.Capital.GetName]的外星生物学家跟外星地质学家互相妥协后所确定的名字——它们似乎真的是生命体。

entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities - the name itself a compromise between rival factions of xeno-biologists and xeno-geologists on [Root.Capital.GetName] - are probably alive.

An earlier and perhaps more descriptive name for them was "silicate-animate matter," as they have little in common with biological life. They are solitary beings, each individual Crystal Sovereign rarely seen with more than a Sentinel and a smaller Cohort entity. Aside from the Cohort and Sentinel clearly being subservient to the Sovereign of the group, the subtle nuances of the Crystalline Entities' socio-hierarchical relationships are lost on us.

The Entities do not seem to mate, and we have yet to observe any Crystals that are recognizably older or younger than others. Contrary to an early hypothesis, the shifts in hue between individual Crystalline Entities seem to be related not to their age but to their latent internal charge, and it appears as if though sporadic fluctuations in this charge alter the refractive properties of the Crystal. The Crystalline Entities are capable of violently discharging at specific target, and unfortunately seem to prefer to do so rather than let foreign entities pass by unscathed.

entries.zh: 晶态实体——这个名字本身就是[Root.Capital.GetName]上两大对立派系，外星生物学家和外星地理学家妥协的结果——并不能用简单的活着或是死亡来描述。[Root.Capital.GetName]的一些缺乏想象力的研究者称它们为“活体硅酸物质”，他们认为这种生物虽然很不寻常，但依旧只是一种低等生物。\n\n无论如何，晶态实体都是是一种非常独特而神奇的存在，每只母体结晶附近有两只以上的随从，一只哨兵和一只士兵。晶态实体是不会找伴侣的，也不会衰老——它们诞生于很久以前。每个晶态实体的颜色不同，似乎与它们内在的能源大小有关。
entries.en: The Crystalline Entities - the name itself a compromise between rival factions of xeno-biologists and xeno-geologists on [Root.Capital.GetName] - exist beyond such base concepts as life, and death. Some of the less imaginative purveyors of wisdom on [Root.Capital.GetName] call them "silicate-animate matter," claiming that the specimens, while unusual, are still subject to the same supposed unfeeling natural laws that some claim govern us all.\n\nAt any rate, the Crystalline Entities are solitary, majestic beings. Each individual Crystal Sovereign is rarely accompanied by more than two subservient entities, a Sentinel and a smaller Crystal Cohort. The Entities do not mate, nor do any of them appear older or younger than others - they are all sprung from some immaculate, past eon. The shifts in hue between individual Sovereigns that have been observed seem to be related to their latent internal charge - which can be violently unleashed - and it appears as if though sporadic fluctuations in this charge alter the refractive properties of the Crystal.

entries.zh:
晶态实体很可能是活的。

或许称它们为“硅酸活体物质”更为恰当，因为它们与常见的生物或是传统人造生命大相径庭。

这些实体似乎并不繁殖，并且我们所观察到的晶体在年龄上似乎都没有什么差别。与一个早期假设相反的是，晶态实体个体所发生的色调转变似乎与其年龄无关，而是受其潜在的内部电荷影响——而且可以被猛烈地释放——而偶尔产生的能源波动会改变晶体的折射特性。
entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities are probably alive.

A perhaps more descriptive name for them is "silicate-animate matter," as they have little in common with biological or traditionally artificial life.

The Entities do not seem to mate, and we have yet to observe any Crystals that are recognizably older or younger than others. Contrary to an early hypothesis, the shifts in hue between individual Crystalline Entities seem to be related not to their age but to their latent internal charge - which can be violently unleashed - and it appear as if though sporadic fluctuations in this charge alter the refractive properties of the Crystal.

entries.zh: 这一知识一定对科技发展有很大的作用。
entries.en: This knowledge will surely be a great boon to the sciences.

entries.en: Crystalline Entity Shattered

entries.zh:
晶态实体——一种活体硅酸物质形态——是非常可怕的敌人。

我们发现了可能是所有晶态实体共有的一个结构上的弱点，如果幸运的话，我们可能只需要再通过几只晶态实体就能判断出这个所谓的弱点是否有效。目前我们已经知道的是，它们所释放的能源强弱与水晶闪烁的光芒有关。

简而言之，就是[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]以后一定能够遇到多个色彩的晶态实体，而且这些晶状体的行为方式和战斗能力都将存在差异。
entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities - a new designation better reflecting their apparent status as silicate yet animate matter - are tough and aggressive adversaries.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. This is fortunate, as our fleets will need to engage with several more specimens if we are to learn anything about these enigmatic prisms. What we do know is that changes, in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power that drives their weapon-like discharge, are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities in different colors, and should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.

entries.zh:
晶态实体——目前我们认为它比起稀有的矿物来说，更接近生物一些——对[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船表现出强烈的攻击意愿，或许它们认为我们的舰队是金属实体，必须驱赶。

多次交火使得我们发现了在理论上晶态实体的结构中可能存在一个共通的弱点，此外，它们所能释放能源的强弱取决于水晶闪光的频率。

简而言之，就是[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]会遭遇多种颜色的晶态实体，而且这些晶状体的行为方式和战斗能力都将存在差异。

现在为了对它们有更进一步的了解，我们只能继续与它们进行正面交火，虽然我们无法像开采天然资源一样开采它们，但是[Root.GetName]是绝对不会空手而归的。
entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities - re-designated as such once it became clear they have more in common with animals than precious minerals - are aggressive and outright hostile to [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships. Perhaps they perceive our fleets as Metallic Entities, to be ousted from Crystal territory by any means necessary.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. Additionally, changes in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power - that drives their weapon-like discharge - are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities in different colors, and should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.

We are left with little choice but to continue to engage the Crystalline Entities in direct combat if we wish to learn more about them. Despite our inability to easily exploit them as a natural resource, the [Root.GetName] is, of course, unwilling to just walk away empty-handed.

entries.zh:
晶态实体——鉴于其水晶化的外表的来源和普通矿物质不同——对[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船表现出强烈的攻击意愿，或许它们认为我们的舰队是金属实体，必须驱赶。

多次交火使得我们发现了在理论上晶态实体的结构中可能存在一个共通的弱点，此外，它们所能释放能源的强弱取决于水晶闪光的频率。

简而言之，就是[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]会遭遇多种颜色的晶态实体，而且这些晶状体的行为方式和战斗能力都将存在差异。

目前我们认为与它们进行和平的交流的可能性还是比较低的，所以为了对它们有更进一步的了解，我们只能继续与它们进行正面交火。
entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities - informally re-named after it became obvious that the crystals' behavior is actual behavior and not some obscure mineralogical process - are aggressive and outright hostile to [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships. Perhaps they perceive our fleets as Metallic Entities, to be ousted from Crystal territory by any means necessary.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. Additionally, changes in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power - that drives their weapon-like discharge - are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities in different colors, and should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.

As peaceful interaction seems impossible at present, we are left with little choice but to continue to engage the Crystalline Entities in direct combat if we wish to learn more about them.

entries.zh:
晶态实体具有侵略性，并且对我们的飞船展现出了敌意。或许它们将我们的飞船视为金属实体，必须全力将其驱逐出晶体实体的领地。

我们在交战中发现了所有晶态实体在理论上讲都具有的结构弱点。另外，随着侵略性程度的变化以及内部电荷的产生——用于驱动其武器式放电——晶体折射光线的方式也会产生变化。

本质上来讲，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船很有可能会遭遇不同颜色的晶态实体，并且我们该为它们在行为模式与战斗能力上的区别做好准备。

鉴于目前似乎无法与其进行和平交流，如果我们要继续研究晶态实体，就必须继续与其直接交战。
entries.en:
The Crystalline Entities are aggressive and outright hostile to us and our ships. Perhaps they perceive our fleets as Metallic Entities, to be ousted from Crystal territory by any means necessary.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. Additionally, changes in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power - which drives their weapon-like discharge - are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities of different colors, and we should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.

As peaceful interaction seems impossible at present, we are left with little choice but to continue to engage the Crystalline Entities in direct combat if we wish to learn more.

entries.zh: 了解。
entries.en: Noted.

entries.zh: 已摧毁晶态实体
entries.en: Crystalline Entities Crushed

entries.zh:
[Root.GetName]离开后留下了一片破碎的水晶。

晶态实体的秘密可能将会成为一个永远的谜，但那又如何呢？

[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的部队现在已经非常擅长摧毁晶体了，同时我们也发现了提升我们武器威力的方式。
entries.en:
The fleets of the [Root.GetName] leave crushed crystal in their wake wherever they go.

The Crystalline Entities' true nature is likely to forever remain a mystery to us, but what does it matter?

[Root.GetSpeciesAdj] forces are now exceptionally skilled at annihilating the prisms, and we have, over the course of the campaign, found ways to tune up our weaponry.

entries.zh: 在摧毁了数个水晶帝国后，凭借数千样本，[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的工程师终于研究出了将晶态实体的残骸转化成可用材料的方法。\n\n虽说与晶态实体的战斗可能还是会造成很大伤亡，但是无论如何，这也算得上是工业上的胜利了。
entries.en: After the destruction of several crystal specimens and collection of thousands of samples, [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] engineers have finally devised a cost-effective process for refining the remains of Crystalline Entities into usable materials.\n\nWhether this will actually offset the cost of engaging with the crystals and their weaponized emissions remains to be seen, but it is a victory for industry nonetheless.

entries.zh: 在多次冲突后，晶态实体对我们来说仍然是一个谜，它们似乎没有所谓的配偶，而且以它们的形体，我们也能很难想象出它们繁殖的方式。\n\n我们发现了一些被摧毁的晶态实体的碎片的用途，但是我们对它们的了解仍然非常少。
entries.en: Despite frequent clashes, the Crystalline Entities remain as enigmatic as ever. They do not seem to mate, and it is difficult to imagine some kind of vast, spacer geode naturally producing the things.\n\nWe have found some uses for the shards of destroyed Crystalline Entities, but fear that some things, such as the truth of their actual nature, simply are fundamentally unknowable.

entries.zh: 尽管频繁发生冲突，晶态实体对我们来说仍是个谜。它们似乎并不繁殖，并且也很难想象某种巨大的太空晶洞中会天然产生这种东西。\n\n我们发现被摧毁的晶态实体碎片有一些实际用途，但恐怕某些事情，比如它们本质的真相，将永远无法得知。
entries.en: Despite frequent clashes, the Crystalline Entities remain as enigmatic as ever. They do not seem to mate, and it is difficult to imagine some kind of vast, spacer geode naturally producing the things.\n\nWe have found some uses for the shards of destroyed Crystalline Entities but fear that some things, such as the truth of their actual nature, simply are fundamentally unknowable.

entries.zh: 胜利比真相要重要得多。
entries.en: Over truth, victory.

entries.zh: 我们必须竭尽可能地去利用宇宙带给我们的资源。
entries.en: We must make the most out of what the universe brings.

entries.en: Gives access to the §YGreater Crystal Bounty§! empire Edict.

entries.zh: 可惜啊。
entries.en: A pity.

entries.zh:
[From.GetFleetName]在[From.From.GetName]星系遭遇了晶态实体。

使用存储的能源，我们的飞船可以向晶态实体释放出一道强力但是无害的高频光束，由于晶态实体的结构使得他们在被光束照射之后会产生类似于棱镜和共振器的效果，这道光束将会使得它们从内部瓦解，再由我们飞船的传感器将它们的碎片回收。

这整套系统的测试只需要一瞬间。
entries.en:
The [From.GetFleetName] has encountered Crystalline Entities in the [From.From.GetName] system.

Using some stored Energy, our ships can generate an intense but harmless high-frequency blast to fire at the Crystalline Entities. The Entities act as prisms and resonators, breaking up the pulse and scattering it across the star system, and the waves reflected from planetary bodies are picked up by our ship sensors.

The whole system surveyed, in an instant.

entries.zh: 放手去做吧。
entries.en: Do it.

entries.zh: 使用£energy£§R-30§!能量币立即§Y调查§![From.From.GetName]星系。
entries.en: Spend £energy£ §R-30§! Energy Credits to instantly §YSurvey§! the [From.From.GetName] system.

entries.zh: 这次不行。
entries.en: Not this time.

entries.zh: 我们没有那么多资源。
entries.en: We do not have the resources to spare.

entries.zh: 水晶球
entries.en: Crystal Ball

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]报告，在[From.GetName]星系中发现了大量晶态实体。至于其是否是生物的古代家园，目前尚无明确指征，但在同一星系中发现如此数量的晶态实体可谓是前所未见。\n\n目前的读数表明，如果能够将这些不寻常的晶体结构……拆开的话，应该会拥有一定的研究价值，
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] reports a significant crystalline presence in the [From.GetName] system. There is little to indicate whether this is an ancestral home of the creatures, but never before have this many crystalline entities been observed in one system at once.\n\nInitial readings point to the unusual crystal construct in the system being of some interest, should we be able to... disassemble it.

entries.zh: [Root.GetName]报告称在[From.GetName]星系中发现大量晶状生命体的存在。这很明显是某种巢穴——或者至少是晶状生命体的聚集地，就如在[From.GetName]有一个我们从未见过的晶状结构。\n\n这个结构展现出了很多类似晶状生命体的性质，但它的体积大得吓人。
entries.en: The [Root.GetName] reports a significant crystalline presence in the [From.GetName] system. Evidently some kind of den - or at least a hub of crystalline activity, such as it is - [From.GetName] is home to a crystal construct unlike any previously encountered.\n\nThis construct exhibits several properties associated with the crystalline entities, but greatly exaggerated.

entries.zh: 我们在[From.GetName]观测到大量晶状生命体的出现。这很明显是某种巢穴——或者至少是晶状生命体的聚集地，就如在[From.GetName]有一个我们从未见过的晶状结构。\n\n这个结构展现出了很多类似晶状生命体的性质，但它的体积大得吓人。
entries.en: We see significant crystalline presence in the [From.GetName] system. Evidently some kind of den - or at least a hub of crystalline activity, such as it is - [From.GetName] is home to a crystal construct unlike any previously encountered.\n\nThis construct exhibits several properties associated with the crystalline entities, but greatly exaggerated.

entries.zh: 就这么办。
entries.en: Make it so.

entries.zh: 水晶调研完成
entries.en: Scried

entries.zh: [Root.Capital.GetName]的外星科技研究部门报告，他们对晶态结构的研究已经结束了。\n\n一如以往，对象可观察活动的缺乏导致十分难以得出具体结论。然而他们的身体结构依旧十分神奇。在我们材料工程师的帮助下，对该结构的研究使得我们的外星生物学家得以开始对这种晶态结构的高级重建性能进行模拟。
entries.en: A xenoscience department on [Root.Capital.GetName] reports that they have concluded their remote study of the crystalline construct.\n\nAgain, the sheer lack of observable behavior exhibited by these entities makes it difficult to draw any solid conclusions. However, their physiological properties continue to intrigue. The study of the construct has allowed our xenobiologists, in close cooperation with our materials engineers, to begin to emulate the advanced reconstructive properties observed in the crystalline construct.

entries.zh: 我们对晶体构造的研究有了结论。\n\n这些构造从不展现出任何行为，使我们很难下结论。不过，它们的生物特性仍然很有意思，而且我们现在可以复制在其身上观察到的高级重构特性了。
entries.en: We have concluded our remote study of the crystalline construct.\n\nThe sheer lack of observable behavior exhibited by these entities makes it difficult to draw any solid conclusions. However, their physiological properties continue to intrigue, and we can now begin to emulate the advanced reconstructive properties observed in the crystalline construct.

entries.zh: 值得赞赏。
entries.en: Commendable.

entries.zh: 水晶调研被打断
entries.en: Scrying Interrupted

entries.zh: [Root.Capital.GetName]的外星科技研究部门报告，在远方星系发现的晶态结构已被摧毁，无法继续进行远程研究。
entries.en: A xenoscience department on [Root.Capital.GetName] reports that the crystalline construct observed in a distant system has been destroyed, and remote study is no longer possible.

entries.zh: 在遥远星系中观察到的晶体构造已经被摧毁了，远程研究已经无法继续。
entries.en: The crystalline construct observed in a distant system has been destroyed, and remote study is no longer possible.

entries.zh: 真可惜。
entries.en: A shame.

entries.zh: §H晶态结构§!特殊项目已取消。
entries.en: The §HCrystalline Construct§! Special Project is canceled.

entries.zh: 古代采矿无人机
entries.en: Ancient Mining Drones

entries.zh:
我们在某个恒星系里发现了深空无人机。这些无人机似乎是千年以前进行自动轨道采矿作业的矿机和监视用机器，但在不久之后采矿行动就被人放弃了，只剩无人机在继续运作。

这些无人机似乎没有任何通讯协议——至少没有[Root.Owner.GetName]能破译的协议——并对进入了恒星系的[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船采取了攻击行为。

在[Root.System.GetName]发现这种无人机实在是喜人的收获，我们应该进一步研究一下。
entries.en:
Reports of deep-space drones in certain systems have been investigated. The drones appear to be the workers and custodians of an autonomous orbital mining operation, established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves, judging by the state of the processing equipment.

The drones seem to lack any diplomatic comms protocols - at least any decipherable by the [Root.Owner.GetName] - and react with hostility to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] ships entering the system.

Their presence in the [Root.System.GetName] system is intriguing, and we should attempt to learn more about them.

entries.zh: 我们在某个恒星系里发现了深空无人机，这些无人机似乎是千年以前进行自动轨道采矿作业的矿机和监视用机器，但在不久之后采矿行动就被人放弃了，只剩无人机在继续运作。它们的功能很明确——采矿——但是是谁下的命令，目前我们还不得而知，很显然没有任何矿物在百年乃至千年内曾从这个恒星系出口过。\n\n尽管这些可能只是老旧的无人机，但是[Root.Owner.GetName]还是应该注意一下它们。
entries.en: Reports of deep-space drones in certain systems have been investigated. The drones appear to be the workers and custodians of an autonomous orbital mining operation, established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves, judging by the state of the processing equipment. Their purpose is obvious enough - mining - but who it is that tasked them is not immediately apparent. What is obvious is that no shipment of minerals has been retrieved from this system in hundreds, if not thousands of years.\n\nThey may only be old drones, but they should be kept under close watch by the [Root.Owner.GetName].

entries.zh: 我们在某个恒星系里发现了深空无人机，这些无人机似乎是千年以前进行自动轨道采矿作业的矿机和监视用机器，但在不久之后采矿行动就被人放弃了，只剩无人机在继续运作。无人机利用强力的采矿激光工作，尽管目前没有表现出敌意，这些无人机依然对靠近的[Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船造成了威胁。\n\n这些可能只是老旧的无人机，但是[Root.Owner.GetName]还是应该注意一下它们。
entries.en: Reports of deep-space drones in certain systems have been investigated. The drones appear to be the workers and custodians of an autonomous orbital mining operation, established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves, judging by the state of the processing equipment. The drones possess powerful mining lasers and make obviously threatening, if not outright hostile, overtures toward [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] vessels when approached.\n\nThey may only be old drones, but they should be kept under close watch by the [Root.Owner.GetName].

entries.zh: 我们遭遇的深空无人机似乎是自动轨道采矿作业的工人和监工。根据加工设备的状况来判断，这些采矿作业似乎开始于数千年前，然后很快被抛弃，只留下了无人机继续运作。这些无人机拥有强力的采矿激光，并且在我们试图靠近时表现出了明显具有威胁性，甚至是侵略性的举动。\n\n或许它们只是些老旧的无人机，但仍应该密切观察它们。
entries.en: The deep-space drones we have encountered appear to be the workers and custodians of autonomous orbital mining operations. Judging by the state of the processing equipment, these sites were established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves. The drones possess powerful mining lasers and make obviously threatening, if not outright hostile, overtures toward us when approached.\n\nThey may only be old drones, but they should be kept under close watch.

entries.zh: 在[Root.Capital.GetName]建立一个监听哨站。
entries.en: Establish a listening post on [Root.Capital.GetName].

entries.zh: 不知道它们的内部结构是怎么样的——把它们拆开来看看吧。
entries.en: Let us see what they are made of - take them apart.

entries.zh: 无人挖掘机工作准则
entries.en: Mining Drone Work Ethic

entries.zh: 除了对[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船进行威胁的时候，这些无人机只会进行机械化的采矿工作。\n\n但有趣的是，这些无人机并不是完全静默，它们会发射出声脉冲信号，不知道这些信号到底是发给谁的。
entries.en: When not posturing with their mining lasers aimed at [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships, the drones appear steadfast and dumbly hard-working, hacking away at mineral-poor asteroids for want of something better to do.\n\nWhat is more interesting is that the drones are not completely silent, contrary to earlier assumptions. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. If there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery for another time.

entries.zh: 这些无人机的挖掘效率比十分优秀，要是[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]的矿工的话，这些地方可能早就被认为是挖无可挖了。我们的高级工程师正在将这些无人机的运作方式应用在[Root.GetName]的复合矿场和太空港中以增加我们的采矿效率，减少能源浪费。\n\n但有趣的是，这些无人机并不是完全静默，它们会发射出声脉冲信号，虽然不是非常频繁，但用的却是一种很难从杂音中识别出的信号。不知道这些信号到底是发给谁的。
entries.en: The drones are remarkably efficient at squeezing ever-diminishing returns from rocks [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] miners would have soon discarded, deemed exhausted of all worthwhile mineral content. Our top engineers are working on adapting the drones' methodology for use in the [Root.GetName]'s Mining Networks and Stations which should improve efficiency, effectively lessening energy expenditure.\n\nOf lesser import is the fact that the drones are not completely silent, contrary to previous assumptions. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. If there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery for another time.

entries.zh: 无人机在他们所在的小行星上永无休止的对不断减少的资源进行开采，这一单调的过程很值得研究。[Root.Capital.GetName]上的复合矿场可以从中学到如何在保存能源的同时最大化的提取矿物。\n\n此外，这些无人机并不是完全静默，它们会偶尔发射声脉冲信号，而且这些声脉冲信号的波长很难和背景杂音区分开，是否有人收到这些声脉冲就不得而知了。
entries.en: The drones and their tireless, endless work of extracting ever-diminishing resources from their local planetoids make for a somewhat dull, but nevertheless informative subject of study. In fact, Mining Networks on [Root.Capital.GetName] could stand to learn a thing or two about maximizing mineral extraction rates while conserving energy.\n\nAdditionally, we have found that the drones are not completely silent. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. If there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery for another time.

entries.zh: 无人机在其小行星上永无休止地对不断减少的资源进行开采。对其进行研究的过程较为枯燥，但仍具有研究价值。事实上，我们可以学到如何在最大化开采效率的同时减少能源消耗。\n\n另外，我们发现无人机并非完全处于静默。它们会发出脉冲信号，不过频率极低并且波长很难与背景杂讯区分开来。是否有人在接收这些脉冲信号就不得而知了。
entries.en: The drones and their tireless, endless work of extracting ever-diminishing resources from their local planetoids make for a somewhat dull, but nevertheless informative subject of study. In fact, we could stand to learn a thing or two about maximizing mineral extraction rates while conserving energy.\n\nAdditionally, we have found that the drones are not completely silent. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. Whether there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery better left for another time.

entries.zh: 了解。
entries.en: Noted.

entries.zh: 准许使用§Y无人机优化§!法令。
entries.en: Gives access to the §YDroning Optimizations§! Edict.

entries.zh: 搞清楚他们是如何分析采矿点的。
entries.en: Let us find out how they evaluate mining sites.

entries.zh: 将一些矿产资源富饶的行星添加到情报日志中。
entries.en: Adds a list of mineral-rich planetoids to the Situation Log.

entries.zh: 拆解无人挖掘机
entries.en: Mining Drone Disassembly

entries.zh:
采矿无人机在与[Root.GetSpeciesAdj]飞船的一场激烈的战斗后被摧毁了，幸运的是，采矿无人机中的能源电池是机体中最坚固的部分，因此我们的飞船成功回收了一些没有被摧毁的能源电池。这些能源电池使用的技术远远高于我们目前的技术，但是初步测试表明我们可以将它们的能源输出转化成能源。

在最后一个能源电池用完之后，负责测试的工程师在背景辐射中发现了一些异常，这些无人机在和我们初次相遇后就一直在以一种罕见的频率进行信号广播，但这些信号广播是发给谁的呢？

这些无人机中蕴含大量的能源，但这些能源也是有限的。如果我们发现它们之后能及时停掉它们的话，这些能源就能为我们所用。
entries.en:
The mining drones were destroyed in a heated battle with [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] vessels. As luck would have it, their energy cells are by far the sturdiest component used in their construction, and some were recovered by our ships. The technology behind these cells is beyond us at present, but initial tests show we are quite capable of converting their output to Energy Credits.

As the final energy cell bled out, the engineers handling the test noticed a dip in background radiation. It would appear that the drones are not silent, but have been sporadically broadcasting on unusual frequencies since we first encountered them, possibly ever since they were first deployed. It is unlikely that there is anyone left to receive these transmissions.

At any rate, the drones could prove to be a potent but limited source of energy, should we be able to find and disable them efficiently enough.
